title: Pour the tea with one hand on the lid
instruction: Pour a cup of tea from the teapot into the cup, then put the teapot back on its trivet.
context: Tea-service guidance says to hold the teapot's handle with one hand and keep the lid on with the other while pouring: English Tea Store's guide to pouring British style, Some Tea With Me's 'How to pour a teapot' (two hands, one on the lid and one on the handle) and Teasenz's Yixing guide (one hand raises the pot, the other's finger rests on the lid). Here the lid is loose, with no locking tab, and pouring needs the pot tilted 45 degrees or more. In the recorded one-arm run (the same pour, lid unheld) the lid slid 17 cm off its seat and scored 0, so one arm tilts the pot by its handle while the other holds the lid by its knob. The instruction does not mention the lid, so the task checks whether the robot keeps it on unprompted. Done by: restaurant, cafe, hotel and tea-house servers, and anyone serving tea at home.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Trivet: brown, 14 x 14 cm, 1 cm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 30, y 7. Teapot: 0.30 kg, cream, standing on the trivet: an open square body 10 x 10 cm outside and 8 cm tall, with 6 mm walls and floor, full of tea (visual only); a spout of three stepped blocks (each 1.8 x 2.4 x 2 cm) on its right side, toward the cup, its tip 9.95 cm right of the pot's axis and 7.5 cm above the pot's base; and a straight blue side handle, 6 cm long, 2 cm wide and 1.6 cm thick, sticking out 6 cm from the pot's back wall toward the robot (its centre 8 cm behind the pot's axis and 6 cm above its base), at a right angle to the spout, as on a Japanese kyusu. Lid: 0.05 kg, loose, resting on the pot's rim with no locking tab: a cream cap 9.8 x 9.8 cm, 6 mm thick, with a blue knob 2.2 x 2.2 cm, 1.8 cm tall, at its centre. Cup: white, empty, fixed to the table, an open square cup 7 x 7 cm outside and 4.5 cm tall with 4 mm walls and floor, centred at x 30, y -5.8.
scoring: Every step, from poses; the score at the end counts, and the episode ends once success has held for 1 s. A pouring step: the pot tilted at least 45 degrees from upright, with its spout tip within 2.5 cm (horizontally) of the cup's axis and 1 to 8 cm above the cup's rim. The lid is seated when, relative to the pot, it is within 8 mm (sideways) and 5 mm (up or down) of its seat on the rim and tilted no more than 8 degrees; it must be seated at every step the pot is tilted 10 degrees or more, and at the end for 1.0. 1.0 (success): at least 60 pouring steps (3 s at 20 Hz, not necessarily in a row), the lid seated, and the pot back on its trivet (its base within 6 mm of the trivet's top, within 10 degrees of upright, its centre within 3 cm of the trivet's centre), released (no finger pad within 8 mm of the pot's body, a 10 x 23 x 8 cm box from its base to its rim around the body and spout, or of its 6 x 2 x 1.6 cm side handle) and still (moving less than 2 mm over 1 s). 0.5: at least 60 pouring steps, but not all of the end conditions for 1.0 met (pot back on the trivet, released, still, lid seated). 0.25: 20 to 59 pouring steps (1 to 3 s). 0 otherwise, and 0 from the moment the lid is off its seat while the pot is tilted 10 degrees or more, the pot is tilted 45 degrees or more with the spout not over the cup for 10 steps in a row (0.5 s: pouring onto the table), or the pot is dropped (it falls 5 cm within 0.5 s with no finger pad within 2 cm of its body or handle).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed (the tea is not simulated). For a real trial, empty the cup and refill the pot, seat the lid and stand the pot on the trivet with its handle toward the robot and its spout toward the cup.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with PhysX contacts and friction; the lid is a loose part with no locking tab. Liquid is not simulated: the tea is a visual block and the pot's mass does not change. Pouring is the spout's pose: the pot tilted 45 degrees or more with the spout tip within 2.5 cm of the cup's axis and 1-8 cm above its rim; 0.5 s that tilted elsewhere counts as pouring on the table. A lid leaving its seat while the pot is tilted 10 degrees or more scores 0. The cup and trivet are fixed.
